First, multiplying each component of $c$ by $-\frac{1}{3}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{3}c & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -6 \\ 12 \\ 9 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -4 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,.\end{aligned}
$$

To compute the dot product, we add up the products of corresponding components:

$$
\begin{aligned}(-\frac{1}{3}c)\cdot d & =0\cdot 9+2\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 6 \\  & =0+8+8-3-6 \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$
